name: Question 4
problem:
For the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}8 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}],$ find the pseudoinverse ${A}^{+}.$
worked_solution:
For an "almost" zero $m\times n$ matrix with non-zero entries 

$$
{\sigma }_{1},\,{\sigma }_{2},\,…,\,{\sigma }_{r}
$$

on the main diagonal, the corresponding pseudoinverse is the "almost" zero $n\times m$ matrix with entries 

$$
{\sigma }_{1}^{-1},\,{\sigma }_{2}^{-1},\,…,\,{\sigma }_{r}^{-1}
$$

on the main diagonal.

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{+} & ={[\begin{aligned}8 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{+} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{8}^{-1} & 0 \\ 0 & {4}^{-1} \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{8}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

For the matrix A=[800040], find the pseudoinverse A+.

a
18[201100]
b
14[100200]
c
18[100200]
d
12[200400]
e
18[200100]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For an "almost" zero m×n matrix with non-zero entries

σ1,σ2,…,σr

on the main diagonal, the corresponding pseudoinverse is the "almost" zero n×m matrix with entries

σ1−1,σ2−1,…,σr−1

on the main diagonal.

Therefore, we obtain

A+=[800040]+=[8−1004−100]=18[100200].
